106.0.0.en: Praise ye the Lord. O give thanks unto the Lord; for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.

106.0.1.en: This Psalm begins with the praise of God because He is good and merciful for ever; for His nature is mercy and goodness. Therefore the heart rejoices at this and begins with rejoicing; because man is a sinner and in need of God's forgiveness and mercy, as will appear from the details of this Psalm. And these sins call man to humility, and to singing of God's mercies.

106.1.0.en: 2- Who can utter the mighty acts of the Lord? who can shew forth all his praise? 3- Blessed are they that keep judgment, and he that doeth righteousness at all times.

106.1.1.en: 1- The writer of the Psalm asks, in the midst of the congregation of the believers, who can speak of God's great power and declare God's praises? And he answers in (v. 3) that the one who can praise God and declare His power is the one who keeps the truth, and always does righteousness. And he is the one who obeys the truth; that is, keeps His commandments.

106.1.2.en: 2- "He that doeth righteousness at all times" is a clear prophecy about Christ, and the believers in Him join Him, those who enjoy fellowship with Him, that is, the saints, so they are able to praise God with all their hearts.

106.1.3.en: And everyone who strives in the way of righteousness and the keeping of the commandments advances in the way of praise, that is, praise is not words that the mouth repeats, but a life that a person lives, so he speaks of the greatness of God and glorifies Him.

106.2.0.en: 4- Remember me, O Lord, with the favour that thou bearest unto thy people: O visit me with thy salvation; 5- That I may see the good of thy chosen, that I may rejoice in the gladness of thy nation, that I may glory with thine inheritance.

106.2.1.en: 1- The writer of the Psalm feels his weakness, because he does not do righteousness at all times; therefore he asks God to remember him with the favour toward His people; that is, to be pleased with him; because God is merciful and loves His people. And he also asks for God's help, so he asks Him to visit him with His salvation, that is, to care for him and support him, so that he may keep the truth and do righteousness. Then he enters into tasting the fellowship with God which the chosen enjoy; not only on earth, but rather in heaven, and then he rejoices greatly and glories in God's mercy and kindnesses with all the believers who have received the eternal inheritance.

106.2.2.en: 2- The writer of the Psalm sees with the eye of prophecy the Apostles and the believers of the New Testament, who enjoy the sight of Christ and the work of the Holy Spirit in the Church, where there are many spiritual good things that gladden the heart, and in which everyone who receives them glories. So he longs for the Incarnation of Christ, and the sight of the New Testament, and the birth of the Church.

106.2.3.en: I wish, my brother, that you would care about keeping God's commandments and applying them in your life, so that you may be satisfied and your tongue be set free to praise Him in the Church, and in your closet, and everywhere.

106.3.s.en: (2) Rebellion in Egypt and the wilderness of Sinai

106.3.0.en: 6- We have sinned with our fathers, we have committed iniquity, we have done wickedly. 7- Our fathers understood not thy wonders in Egypt; they remembered not the multitude of thy mercies; but provoked him at the sea, even at the Red sea.

106.3.1.en: The Sea of Suph: the Red Sea.

106.3.2.en: 1- With feelings of repentance and regret the writer of the Psalm declares on behalf of the people of God that they rebelled against God many times, and offended Him through the rebellion of the fathers. And the first rebellion was after their departure from the land of Egypt and their arrival at the Sea of Suph, when they saw Pharaoh with his army coming toward them.

106.3.3.en: So they murmured against Moses saying: Are there no graves in Egypt that you brought us out to die in the wilderness before the Sea of Suph? Did we not say to you: Leave us to live in the wilderness of Egypt, it is better than dying in the wilderness (Ex 14:11, 12).

106.3.4.en: 2- This murmuring of the children of Israel took place after they had seen God's wonders in the ten plagues with which He struck the Egyptians, and at the same time His mercy on His people, which kept them from these plagues. They saw the wonders but did not understand them, and this is what happens with us to this day, for we see God's works with us but we do not understand, so we are agitated and anxious and murmur.

106.4.0.en: 8- Nevertheless he saved them for his name's sake, that he might make his mighty power to be known. 9- He rebuked the Red sea also, and it was dried up: so he led them through the depths, as through the wilderness. 10- And he saved them from the hand of him that hated them, and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy. 11- And the waters covered their enemies: there was not one of them left. 12- Then believed they his words; they sang his praise.

106.4.1.en: The depths: the many waters; what is meant by it is the depths of the sea.

106.4.2.en: 1- In the face of the people's rebellion we did not see God's wrath, but on the contrary His power in saving them from Pharaoh and his army, for He rebuked the sea by means of Moses' striking the sea with his rod, so it was divided and the depths of the sea were uncovered, and became dry land like the wilderness, and the people of God crossed over in it to the other shore.

106.4.3.en: But Pharaoh and his army, who dared and pursued the children of Israel and did not fear their God who had struck them with the ten plagues, when Moses struck the sea a second time it returned as it was, and Pharaoh and all his army were drowned, and all of them died, and it was the strongest army in the world at that time; because Egypt was the first empire in the world, and it controlled those around it. So the children of Israel rejoiced and sang to God with thanksgiving and believed in Him.

106.4.4.en: 2- As God saved His people the children of Israel from the slavery of the Egyptians by their crossing the Red Sea and the drowning of Pharaoh and his soldiers; so also He saves His children in the New Testament from the slavery of Satan by their crossing through the water of Baptism, so they receive the new nature and the freedom of the children of God.

106.5.0.en: 13- They soon forgat his works; they waited not for his counsel: 14- But lusted exceedingly in the wilderness, and tempted God in the desert. 15- And he gave them their request; but sent leanness into their soul.

106.5.1.en: 1- Three days had not passed since their crossing the Red Sea and the drowning of Pharaoh when they murmured because of their thirst when they reached the region of Elim, and they did not seek God's counsel by prayer and supplication because the waters were bitter. But Moses prayed, and God guided him to throw a tree into the water, and it turned into sweet water (Ex 15:22-24). And they murmured also after this asking for meat, so He gave them quails and they were satisfied with them, for they ate greedily, but God struck them with serpents and their bodies and souls fell into leanness. And when they cried out to God, Moses made the bronze serpent, and saved them from death when they looked at it (Num 11).

106.5.2.en: 2- The tree is a symbol of the cross, which turns bitterness into sweetness, and the bronze serpent is a symbol of the crucified Christ, who saves us from the death of sin and lust.

106.6.0.en: 16- They envied Moses also in the camp, and Aaron the saint of the Lord. 17- The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan, and covered the company of Abiram. 18- And a fire was kindled in their company; the flame burned up the wicked.

106.6.1.en: 1- Korah, Dathan and Abiram, and two hundred and fifty men who followed them, envied and murmured against Moses and Aaron for their being singled out for the priesthood and speaking with God, so God was angry with them, and the earth was split open and swallowed them, and the fire also burned them; that God might show the greatness of His children and that all the people might revere the priesthood.

106.6.2.en: 2- Moses was a type of Christ as the leader of His people, and Aaron also is a type of Christ our greatest High Priest. And the splitting of the earth and the swallowing of the wicked shows the providence of God, who established the earth for the sake of His children but it shakes, and splits and swallows the wicked. And the fire shows God's wrath, because our God is a consuming fire, and it is a symbol of the eternal fire.

106.7.0.en: 19- They made a calf in Horeb, and worshipped the molten image. 20- Thus they changed their glory into the similitude of an ox that eateth grass.

106.7.2.en: Although the people of God in Sinai asked to see God, and God appeared to them on the mountain in a great sight, and they were very afraid, and said to Moses: You go up and speak with God and tell us. And after he went up and was absent forty days with God, they thought that he had died, or that some strange thing had happened to him, so they turned back from the worship of God, and asked for another god. So Aaron made them a golden calf to worship. And instead of worshipping God who dwells in heaven they debased themselves and made an image of an animal that eats the people; that is, the calf. It is a very strange rebellion and debasement of thought, and they resembled the surrounding nations in the worship of idols, such as Egypt.

106.8.0.en: 21- They forgat God their saviour, which had done great things in Egypt; 22- Wondrous works in the land of Ham, and terrible things by the Red sea. 23- Therefore he said that he would destroy them, had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach, to turn away his wrath, lest he should destroy them.

106.8.1.en: The land of Ham: Ham the son of Noah settled in Egypt and the surrounding countries in Africa, and what is meant here is the land of Egypt.

106.8.2.en: Stood in the breach: interceded and prayed.

106.8.3.en: The rebellion of the people of God in Sinai by worshipping the golden calf is a forgetting of all the great works of God that He did with them to bring them out of the land of Egypt, whether the ten plagues, or the parting of the Red Sea, and their crossing and the drowning of Pharaoh. So it is a terrible rebellion that deserves that God punish them severely and destroy them, had not Moses stood praying and interceding for his people, so God forgave them (Deut 9:25-29), and this shows the faith of Moses and his boldness before God, for he stood praying for a stubborn people, standing before God who was angry with his people.

106.8.4.en: So God's love and long-suffering appeared, and His great esteem for intercession, and He forgave the people.

106.9.0.en: 24- Yea, they despised the pleasant land, they believed not his word: 25- But murmured in their tents, and hearkened not unto the voice of the Lord. 26- Therefore he lifted up his hand against them, to overthrow them in the wilderness: They murmured: grumbled, rebelled and cried out.

106.9.1.en: When the children of Israel came out of Egypt Moses sent twelve men to spy out the land of Canaan, and they reported that the land was fertile and pleasant, but that its inhabitants were giants who could not be overcome, that is, they did not believe in God, so they refused to enter the pleasant land of Canaan. And none of these wicked spies was an exception except two, Joshua the son of Nun and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, so the people were influenced by the words of doubt because of their unbelief in God, and refused to enter the land of Canaan. So God swore (lifted up His hand) that all those who rebelled would not be permitted to enter and possess the land of Canaan, but must perish in the wilderness of Sinai (Num 14:21-23). And He made them wander forty years in the wilderness until all who had rebelled died, and only their sons, who were children at the time of this rebellion, entered.

106.10.0.en: 27- To overthrow their seed also among the nations, and to scatter them in the lands.

106.10.1.en: But when this generation that entered the land of Canaan rebelled, God commanded that they go into the Assyrian captivity, then the Babylonian, so He dispersed them and scattered them far from their country throughout the Assyrian kingdom, then the Babylonian; until they repented, and then He brought them back to their land.

106.11.0.en: 28- They joined themselves also unto Baalpeor, and ate the sacrifices of the dead. 29- Thus they provoked him to anger with their inventions: and the plague brake in upon them. 30- Then stood up Phinehas, and executed judgment: and so the plague was stayed. 31- And that was counted unto him for righteousness unto all generations for evermore.

106.11.1.en: Baal: the name of a pagan god well known among many nations in the East.

106.11.2.en: Peor: a mountain in Moab, and what is meant by Baalpeor is: the Baal whose worship is found on Mount Peor and who is worshipped by the Moabites.

106.11.3.en: The sacrifices of the dead: the sacrifices offered to dead idols.

106.11.4.en: Executed judgment: that is, judged and decided and intervened to punish the licentious; the Jewish man and the Midianite woman.

106.11.5.en: Balak king of Moab tried - by means of Balaam the prophet the son of Beor - to curse the people of God, but God refused and blessed them. So Balaam advised Balak to throw Moabite girls to the children of Israel to commit fornication with them, so that God would be angry with them and forsake them, and it would be easy for Balak to defeat the children of Israel. And this actually happened, for the children of Israel committed fornication with the Moabite women, and bowed down to their pagan god Baalpeor, and ate of the sacrifices offered to him. So the Lord struck them with the plague, and twenty-four thousand of them died. And Moses and the elders of Israel hurried to the door of the tent of meeting with prayer and supplication and much weeping, but there were some Jews immersed in fornication, so that an Israelite man named Zimri took a pagan Midianite woman before all the people and went into the tent to commit fornication with her. So Phinehas the priest was jealous with the jealousy of God against evil, and took a spear and killed the two adulterers with it, so God's wrath was calmed because of the prayers of Moses and those with him and the zeal of Phinehas, and He stopped the plague, and God blessed Phinehas the priest and his seed (Num 25). From this appears God's hatred of evil and His punishment of it, and on the other hand the power of prayer and the zeal of the righteous, especially those in positions of responsibility.

106.12.0.en: 32- They angered him also at the waters of strife, so that it went ill with Moses for their sakes: 33- Because they provoked his spirit, so that he spake unadvisedly with his lips.

106.12.1.en: Meribah (the waters of strife): a place where there is a rock near the city of Kadesh-barnea, which lies north of the Gulf of Aqaba and south of the Dead Sea and Beersheba; that is, south of the land of Canaan.

106.12.2.en: They angered him: they made him very angry.

106.12.3.en: Spake unadvisedly with his lips: spoke without wisdom.

106.12.4.en: 1- The people of the children of Israel were much given to murmuring and rebellion; until they made Moses very angry when they reached the region south of Kadesh-barnea. So Moses was troubled and uttered words in which there was something of hesitation and doubt, for he said, "Must we fetch you water out of this rock?" Then he struck the rock twice instead of once (Num 20:10). So God was displeased with him and prevented him - and Aaron, who shared with him in this act - from entering the land of Canaan, so the two died before entering Canaan, and Joshua entered with the people as God commanded him.

106.12.5.en: 2- The Psalm here mentions a group of the rebellions of the children of Israel against God, which are:

106.12.6.en: a- Their rebellion when Pharaoh pursued them before they crossed the Red Sea (v. 7).

106.12.7.en: b- Their rebellion because there was no meat in the wilderness of Sinai (v. 14).

106.12.8.en: c- Their rebellion against Moses and Aaron because of their being set apart for the priesthood (v. 16).

106.12.9.en: d- The worship of the golden calf (v. 19).

106.12.10.en: e- Their refusal to enter the land of Canaan because of the words of the spies (v. 24).

106.12.12.en: g- Murmuring because there was no water at Meribah (v. 32).

106.12.13.en: Do not hasten to murmur against God if you do not find what you want, but be patient and persevere in your prayers, and the Lord will give you at the right time your needs, and even pour out upon you more than you ask or think.

106.13.s.en: (3) Rebellion in the land of Canaan

106.13.0.en: 34- They did not destroy the nations, concerning whom the Lord commanded them: 35- But were mingled among the heathen, and learned their works. 36- And they served their idols: which were a snare unto them.

106.13.1.en: A snare: a trap and a net.

106.13.2.en: After God brought His people into the land of Canaan He commanded them to destroy the pagans, the inhabitants of the land, because of their evils (Ex 23:32, 33). For God had been very long-suffering toward them and they did not turn back from their evils.

106.13.3.en: But the children of Israel were negligent and did not obey God, so there happened to them what God had warned them of, for they mingled with these pagans, and learned their evil works, that is, their sins, and took part with them in the worship of idols. So their mixing with these pagans became a snare for them that took them far from God. They are rebels against God, who do not obey His commandments but their own whims and desires.

106.14.0.en: 37- Yea, they sacrificed their sons and their daughters unto idols, 38- And shed innocent blood, even the blood of their sons and of their daughters, whom they sacrificed unto the idols of Canaan: and the land was polluted with blood. 39- Thus were they defiled with their own works, and went a whoring with their own inventions.

106.14.1.en: Shed: caused to flow; that is, they made the blood of their sons flow on the ground.

106.14.2.en: Innocent blood: blameless blood, that is, the blood of the innocent and not of the wicked.

106.14.3.en: The mingling of the people of God with the pagans made them imitate them in the most horrible deeds, so that they slaughtered their sons who had done no evil. Although murder is a very great sin, and killing the wicked is easier than killing the innocent, they killed the innocent, and also their beloved sons, to please the ideas of Satan through the pagan gods; thus they left God and His commandments and clung to the wicked; that is, they fell into spiritual fornication, and became unclean. This is the result of rebellion against God.

106.14.4.en: Do not neglect, my brother, God's commandments because of any thought that comes to you and you think it is from your own mind; as long as it is a destructive and disturbing thought, trust that it is from Satan; because God's thoughts and commandments give peace and build up your life. Do not rush into evil, for this is spiritual fornication, but cling to God and you will enjoy His love, His care and His peace.

106.15.s.en: (4) God's punishment and deliverance of His people

106.15.0.en: 40- Therefore was the wrath of the Lord kindled against his people, insomuch that he abhorred his own inheritance. 41- And he gave them into the hand of the heathen; and they that hated them ruled over them. 42- Their enemies also oppressed them, and they were brought into subjection under their hand.

106.15.1.en: When the people of God persisted in evil as a result of their mingling with the pagans, God was angry with them in order to discipline them so that they would repent, so He forsook them, and lifted His protection from them. Then their enemies, with whom they had mingled and shared in evil, ruled over them and humiliated them, and God permitted this; so that by this punishment they would take heed of the seriousness of evil and repent.

106.16.0.en: 43- Many times did he deliver them; but they provoked him with their counsel, and were brought low for their iniquity. 44- Nevertheless he regarded their affliction, when he heard their cry: 45- And he remembered for them his covenant, and repented according to the multitude of his mercies. 46- And he gave them grace before all those that carried them captives.

106.16.1.en: Brought low: they came down from their rank as children of God and became like the wicked.

106.16.3.en: God did not continue to punish His children, but His discipline was temporary so that they might repent, for God looked with His fatherhood and love upon His people and heard their prayers and their cry to Him when their enemies humbled them, so He saved them by His power; because they are His children with whom He made a covenant to protect them. For although they had broken the covenant, by their repentance they returned to God, so He had mercy on them, and even gave them grace before those who had humbled them, so they were lifted up and found rest by the grace of God. As happened in the Babylonian captivity, for when they repented and cried to God He moved the heart of Cyrus king of Media and Persia and he sent them back to their land, and they built the temple of God. And as happened with Daniel and the three young men, for Nebuchadnezzar raised them to be rulers of the kingdom. And likewise when Pharaoh raised Joseph from prison to be ruler over Egypt.

106.17.0.en: 47- Save us, O Lord our God, and gather us from among the heathen, to give thanks unto thy holy name, and to triumph in thy praise. 48- Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting: and let all the people say, Amen. Praise ye the Lord.

106.17.1.en: 1- At the end of the Psalm the people of God cry out to Him, rejecting all rebellion, and declaring their need of Him by saying: save us from every evil and humiliation into which we have cast ourselves. And this is also a prophecy about the request of the captive people of God that He save them and gather them from among the nations. And the aim of the salvation is not only liberation from the humiliation of slavery, but rather life with God, and thanking Him for rescuing them, then praising Him, and even glorying in their sonship to God in the midst of the evil world, and they continue to bless Him throughout their life, indeed for ever.

106.17.2.en: 2- These two verses declare the desire of the children of God in the Old Testament who long for the salvation of Christ and life with Him in the Church of the New Testament. And they are also the feelings of the Church in the New Testament, longing for deliverance from the prison of the body and for rising to the glories of the Kingdom, where there is continual praise.

106.17.3.en: 3- This Psalm is the end of the fourth book of the five books of the Psalms according to the Jewish division. And the fourth section begins from Psalm ninety to Psalm one hundred and six.

106.17.4.en: And we notice the conclusion of this section with (v. 48), which is repeated at the end of each of the four sections. As for the fifth section, this sentence is not written at its end, because it is the end of all the Psalms.

106.17.5.en: Wonderful is Your long-suffering, O God; for You give me successive opportunities for repentance, and bear my disobedience of Your commandments and my immersion in sins. But my hope is Your mercy, O Lord, for I have no Savior but You, so have mercy on me; for I need Your fatherhood, indeed I long to live for You, and praise You and enjoy fellowship with You, for this is the true life, and not the evil desires of the world.

106.17.6.en: God's care for His children: "O give thanks unto the Lord, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever. Let the redeemed of the Lord say so, whom he hath redeemed from the hand of the enemy" (vv. 1, 2) Introduction:

106.17.7.en: 1- Its writer: It has no title, so it is counted among the "orphan" Psalms whose writer is not known. And some attribute this Psalm to David.

106.17.8.en: 2- When was it written? There are two opinions:

106.17.9.en: a- That it was written a little after the return from the captivity, and they rely on the words "the redeemed of the Lord"

106.17.10.en: (v. 2), that is, those returning from the captivity, whom He redeemed from slavery.

106.17.11.en: b- That it was written before the captivity by David or another, and it speaks of God's redemption of His people in all the circumstances of their life, and a prophecy of the return from the captivity. And this opinion is the more probable.

106.17.12.en: 3- This Psalm is thanksgiving and praise to God, so it suits every believer who feels the hand of God, especially in the afflictions from which He rescues him, so he lifts up his heart in thanks to Him.

106.17.13.en: 4- There is a relation between this Psalm and the two Psalms before it. The three Psalms speak of the history of the people of God and His work with them, so we see that Psalm 051 tells us of God's care for His children and His carrying out His covenants with them. And Psalm 106 tells us of the rebellion of the people of God against Him and His long-suffering toward them. As for Psalm 107, it tells us of His care for His people and His bringing them out of the various afflictions, even if it was the heavy captivity.

106.17.14.en: 5- This Psalm is the first of the fifth and last book of the Psalms, which begins with this Psalm (107) and ends with Psalm (151). And this fifth book tells us of the living word of God, and among the most important things this book contains:

106.17.15.en: a- Psalm 119, which is David's experiences with the word of God, and it comes in twenty-two parts.

106.17.16.en: b- The Psalms from (120-134), which are called the Psalms of Ascents, which the people of God used to repeat when they went up the mountain in Jerusalem to the temple of God.

106.17.17.en: c- Psalm 136, which the Church calls the Second Hoos. It is a Psalm of thanksgiving to God who cared for His people and cares for them in every generation, and the Church repeats it.

106.17.18.en: d- The Psalms from (148-150), which the Church repeats every day and calls the Fourth Hoos, that is, the fourth praise, and they contain much rejoicing, thanksgiving and praise to God.

106.17.19.en: 6- This Psalm does not occur in the Agpeya.
